attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you type the names of 5-7 of the image variables inside the brackets [ ] of the imageArray?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What should be added inside the brackets of the imageArray array declaration?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In this project, the image variables will be used to place sprites on the screen. The user will gain or lose points depending on whether the images match. Point out to the ninja that fewer variables will make the game easier and more variables will make the game harder.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by reviewing the starter code and storing image variables in an array!


Notice there is already code in the editor; there is a Display sprite kind declared under // sprite kind set up, several image variables declared under // image set up, and additional code comments to organize the project’s code underneath.  

 

Click on the palette icon next to each image variable to view the images that will be used in the match game. 


Underneath // array set up, use the keyword let to declare a new array called imageArray. Type an assignment operator and a pair of brackets [ ], then type 5-7 of the image variable names inside, separated by commas. 


Now, the sprite images are stored in the imageArray to be used in the project.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create 2 variables and use a for loop to create a row of sprites?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How many times will the for loop run? 

❓ How is the loop’s counter variable used in the code that sets each sprite’s x-position?

❓ What might you set the card sprite’s y-position to, so that the sprites appear in the middle of the screen?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk the ninja through the logic of the for loop’s code. The counter variable will begin at 0 and continue increasing by 1 while the count is less than 3, causing the loop to run 3 times. Each time the loop is run, a new card sprite will be created and it will be placed further across the screen. The 3 sprites will appear in a row.

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use screen.height/2 to set the card sprite’s y-position to the middle of the screen.
steps.instructions:
Use variables and a for loop to create a row of 3 card sprites from an array! 


Create 2 new variables to offset and add spacing between each sprite and the side of the screen. Under // game set up, create an xOffset variable set to 40, and a spacing variable named set to 36.


Open Loops and drag [for] underneath the existing code under // game set up.


Change the counter variable i to count in all 3 expressions, then update the run condition to count < 3 so the loop will run 3 times.


Open Sprites and drag [sprite (img) of kind (kind)] inside the curly brackets { } of the for loop. Update the sprite name, then replace img`...` with cardImage 


Set the sprite’s x-position inside the curly brackets { } of the for loop. Multiply the count counter variable and the spacing variable to spread out the 3 sprites. Add the value of xOffset to offset the row of sprites from the left side of the screen.


Set the sprite’s y-position equal to the middle of the screen.


Click ▶ to see the 3 card sprites appear in a row.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use randint to select a random value from the imageArray array between 0 and the length of the imageArray array minus 1?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the A button is pressed? 

❓ Why should 1 be subtracted from the length of the imageArray array in the randint function’s maximum argument?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that the elements in an array are assigned an index, based on the order in which they are added. The index begins at 0, then increases by 1 each time an element is added. 

💡 In this example, the randint function randomly selects a value between 0 and the length of the imageArray array minus 1 to set the sprite’s image. Because the index of elements in the array begin at 0, the third element’s index is 1 less than the length of the array. As a result, 1 needs to be subtracted from the length of the imageArray array, so that the randint function only selects an element with an index found in the array.
steps.instructions:
Generate 3 random sprite images to be displayed on the cards when the A button is pressed!


Open Controller and drag [run code on (button) button (event)] underneath // game events. Use the default property A and default event Pressed.


Open Loops and drag [for] inside the curly brackets { } of the controller.A event. Change the counter variable i to count in all 3 expressions, then update the run condition to count < 3 so the loop will run 3 times.


Open Sprites and drag [sprite (img) of kind (kind)] inside the curly brackets { } of the for loop. Update the display sprite name, and change the sprite kind to Display.


Replace img`...` with imageArray and a pair of brackets [ ]. Inside the brackets [ ], use randint to select a random value from the array between 0 and the length of the imageArray array minus 1.


Copy (CTRL + C) the code that sets the card sprite’s x and y-positions inside the previous for loop, then paste (CTRL + V) it inside the curly brackets { } of the for loop inside the controller.A event. Update the sprite name. 


Click ▶ and press the A button to see the 3 random sprite images appear on the cards!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add the push function to the name of the empty sprite array inside the for loop?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What types of elements can be stored in the displayArray?

❓ What symbols need to be included when declaring an empty array?

❓ What will happen when a new display sprite is created?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that an array can be made up of image, string, number, or sprite values. However, all elements in the array must be of the same type. As a result, it’s important to define what type of elements the empty array will store, so that the program is unable to add different types of elements into the same array.

💡 Make sure the ninja has included a colon :, the type Sprite, and a pair of brackets [ ] before the assignment operator in the displayArray declaration. Point out to the ninja that the Sprite type appears in teal and has a capital S.

💡 Explain to the ninja that each time a Display sprite is created, its value is pushed to the end of the displayArray. These elements will be able to be referenced later in the project.
steps.instructions:
Create an empty array to store the generated sprites!


Underneath // array set up, use the keyword let to declare an empty array of sprites called displayArray. Use : Sprite [] after its name. Then, type an assignment operator and a second pair of brackets [ ].


Inside the curly brackets { } of the for loop inside the controller.A event, add code that will store the 3 Display sprites in the empty displayArray. Type the name of the array and a dot operator . then select push from the code completion tool and type a pair of parentheses ( ). Inside the parentheses, type the name of the Display sprite. 


Now, every time the A button is pressed, the 3 Display sprites will be pushed to the array.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use a destroyAllSpritesOfKind function to destroy all Display sprites inside the curly brackets { } of the controller.A event?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does the destroyAllSpritesOfKind function solve this bug?

❓ What does it mean to assign the displayArray to an empty array? Why is this code needed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Now, the destroyAllSpritesOfKind function will destroy all Display sprites each time the A button is pressed. That means that the previous sprites will be destroyed before new Display sprites are created.

💡 Explain to the ninja that by typing an assignment operator and a pair of brackets to the right of an array’s name, it clears out the elements in the array and resets it. This code is needed in addition to the destroyAllSpritesOfKind function in order for the indices of the elements to remain accurate as new sprites are added to the project, each time the A button is pressed.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The Display sprites are appearing on top of each other. Delete the previous sprites from the screen and remove them from the array each time the A button is pressed.


Inside the curly brackets { } of the controller.A event, create a blank line above the for loop. Open Sprites and drag [destroy all sprites of kind (kind)] onto the blank line. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text:


sprites.destroyAllSpritesOfKind(SpriteKind.Player)


The destroyAllSpritesOfKind function takes 1  parameter: kind. Change the kind parameter to SpriteKind.Display.


Below the destroyAllSpritesOfKind function, reset the displayArray  each time the A button is pressed. Type = [ ] after the array name. 


Click ▶ and press the A button to see new display sprites appear without overlapping with previous display sprites.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you update the value argument of the setScore and changeScoreBy functions?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why might the starting score be a positive number instead of 0?

❓ Why might the score decrease each time the A button is pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that the score will be changed based on whether the display sprites’ images match each other. Each time the A button is pressed, new sprites will appear and the score will decrease to give the user another chance to see matching images!
steps.instructions:
Decrease the score each time the A button is pressed!


Open Info and drag [set score to (value)] underneath // game set up. Change the value argument to 100. 


Inside the curly brackets { } of the controller.A event, create a blank line at the top. Open Info again and drag [change score by (1)] onto the blank line. Change the value argument to a negative amount, such as -25. 


Click ▶ to see the score decrease on each button press!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use a Boolean AND operator && inside the parentheses of the if condition to check if the images of the first, second, and third element of the displayArray are all equal?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓What needs to be true in order for the code inside the if condition to run?

❓ How many points might the score change by when all 3 images are the same?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the image at index 0 of the displayArray is equal to the image at index 1 of the displayArray AND the image at index 0 of the displayArray is equal to the image at index 2 of the displayArray, then the score will increase. 

💡 Explain the logic of the condition to the ninja. By checking if the first image is equal to the second and third images, then the assumption can be made that the second and third images are equal (e.g. if A = B and A = C, then B = C).

💡 Point out to the ninja that an element at a specific index can be found by typing the name of an array followed by a pair of brackets, with the index number inside.
steps.instructions:
Change the score if all 3 display images match!


Open Logic and drag [if else] underneath the for loop inside the controller.A event. Inside the parentheses of the if condition, type displayArray then a pair of brackets [] with 0 inside to access the first element in the array. Type a dot operator then select image from the code completion tool. Use an equality operator == then type the same array code with a 1 inside the brackets to access the second element in the array. The code might look like:

displayArray[0].image == displayArray[1].image

Next, type a Boolean AND operator && inside the parentheses of the if condition to check if the images of the first and third elements are equal. Copy (Ctrl + C) the statement and paste (Ctrl + V) it to the right of &&, then replace the index 1 with 2 to access the third element in the array. 


Open Info and drag [change score by (1)] inside the curly brackets { } of the if condition. Change the value argument to a larger amount, such as 100. 


Click ▶ and press the A button to see the score increase if all 3 images match!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use 2 Boolean OR operators || to check for 3 possible statements to be true?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How do you change an else condition into an else if condition?

❓ What needs to be true in order for the code inside the else if condition to run?

❓ Why do the images at index 1 and index 2 of the displayArray need to be checked in the else if condition?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can change an else condition into an else if condition by typing if followed by a pair of parentheses () and a pair of curly brackets { }.

💡 When the image at index 0 of the displayArray is equal to the image at index 1 of the displayArray OR if the image at index 0 of the displayArray is equal to the image at index 2 of the displayArray OR if the image at index 1 of the displayArray is equal to the image at index 2 of the displayArray, then the score will increase. 

💡 The images at index 1 and index 2 of the displayArray need to be checked in the else if condition because an assumption cannot be made that they are equal. The Boolean OR operator will run the code upon the first instance of a true statement. If the images at index 1 and 2 are being checked, that means that the image at index 0 is not equal to the images at index 1 or index 2.
steps.instructions:
Change the score if 2 of the 3 display images match!


In the if conditional, turn else into an else if condition. Copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) the entire statement from the parentheses of the if condition and replace && with a Boolean OR operator || to check if the image value of the first and second OR first and third elements are the same. 


Type another Boolean OR operator || after the existing statements inside the parentheses. Copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) one of the statements to the right of the || then replace the index values with 1 and 2 to access the second and third elements in the array. 


Open Info and drag [change score by (1)] inside the curly brackets { } of the else if condition. Change the value argument to a smaller amount, such as 50. 


Click ▶ and press the A button to see the score increase if 2 of the 3 images match!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use an operator inside the parentheses of the if condition to check if the score is less than or equal to 0?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What condition needs to be true in order for the game to end in a loss?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 If the score is less than or equal to 0, then the game will end in a loss. The less than or equal to relational operator should be used so that the user’s score does not need to exactly equal 0 in order for the game to end. 

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the setGameOverEffect function before the gameOver function to set an effect to play when the game over screen appears.
steps.instructions:
End the game if the score is equal to 0! 


Open Logic and drag [if] to the bottom of the controller.A event. Inside the parentheses of the if condition, replace true with code that checks if the score is less than or equal to 0. Then, open Game and drag [game over (true)] inside the curly brackets { } of the if conditional and update the parameter to end the game in a loss.


Click ▶ to see the game end if the score is less than or equal to 0.

steps.hints: ❓ What directions would help users understand how the game works?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What background color might you use as a backdrop for the project?

❓ What directions might tell the user how to play the game? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the ninja that they can always click on the palette for one of the images in the code to open the editor. Once opened, they can hover their cursor over each individual color to find the corresponding value to use as a background color.

💡 Remind the ninja that strings need to be placed inside of quotation marks and that parameters need to be separated by a comma, otherwise the code will not be able to run correctly.
steps.instructions:
Finish the project by adding a background color, a dialog frame, and directions!


Open Scene, drag [set background color to (color)] under // game set up. Set a color parameter using a number 1-15.


Open Game and drag [set dialog frame to (frame)] underneath the setBackgroundColor code. Select a dialog frame image from the gallery.


Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] underneath the setDialogFrame code. Update the string and layout parameters, so that the dialog box shares directions for the user to follow.


Click ▶ to see the completed project!

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses arrays to randomly generate 3 images then check for a match!

validationItems.text: Store at least 5 image variables in an imageArray.
Use a for loop to create a row of 3 card sprites from an array.
Use a for loop to generate 3 random sprite images when the A button is pressed.
Create an array to store the generated sprites.
Destroy all Display sprites from the screen and remove them from the array each time the A button is pressed.
Change the score each time the A button is pressed or if the images match.
Use an if statement to see if all three images match.
Use an else if statement to see if 2 of the 3 images match.

requirements.match: displayArray[0].image == displayArray[1].image || displayArray[0].image == displayArray[2].image || displayArray[1].image == displayArray[2].image

validationItems.text: End the game if the score is less than or equal to 0.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and array functions. You’ll build on your understanding of arrays in JavaScript by exploring functions that will help you access, modify, and join elements in an array. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Push It, Pop It, Join It, Concat It!
badges.description: Use several different array functions in JavaScript to access and modify the data stored inside an array.

badges.title: A String of Numbers
badges.description: Use the toString function to convert a number to a string

badges.title: Arrays All The Way Down
badges.description: Create a nested array in JavaScript.

badges.title: Joined at the Hip
badges.description: Use the join function to join all the elements of a string array into one string value.

badges.title: Together Forever
badges.description: Use the concat function to join two arrays together into one new array.

badges.title: Pop It Like It’s Hot
badges.description: Use the pop function to remove and return the last element from an array.

badges.title: Group Project
badges.description: Use the allOfKind function to create an array of all sprites of the specified sprite kind.
